paper.title: Bi-directional ferrite to austenite transformation through warm temperature deformation of a ferrite-based low density steel
paper.paper_scope: Assessing the capability for strain-induced bidirectional ferrite-to-austenite and austenite-to-ferrite transformation in a Fe-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.07C (wt.%) ferrite-based low density steel deformed in compression over a warm temperature range (100–700 °C), combining thermodynamic Gibbs energy modelling with detailed microstructural analysis.

alloys.description: A ferrite-based low density (lightweight) steel received in an electroslag remelted (ESR) condition; designed/used to study strain-induced bidirectional ferrite↔austenite transformation because of its triplex ferrite + austenite + martensite microstructure and high stacking fault energy (80–110 mJ/m^2).
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition quoted as Fe-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.07C (wt.%). Full processing history: ESR → homogenization at 1200 °C/1 h → 5-pass hot rolling at 1100–1200 °C → air quench → annealing at 950 °C/1 h (triplex ferrite + austenite + thermally induced martensite). After deformation at 500 °C to true strain 0.6, SEM composition analysis (Table 1) showed Mn enriched in austenite (12.8±0.1 wt% vs 10.3±0.1 wt% in ferrite) and Al enriched in ferrite (6.0±0.1 wt% vs 4.7±0.1 wt% in austenite). Atomic percentages were not reported.

processes.processes_notes: This is the starting/reference state; all warm compression tests were conducted on this annealed triplex microstructure.

unmapped_findings: Compression tests were carried out over a wide temperature range of 100–700 °C at a strain rate of 0.001 s^-1 up to a true strain of 0.6; specimens were soaked 5 min at the deformation temperature before testing and immediately water quenched afterwards (BLOCK b0016, b0020).

Equilibrium elemental partitioning (Mn, Al) between ferrite and austenite and the Gibbs free energy were calculated with Thermo-Calc using the TCFE9 database; phases predicted were BCC_A2 (ferrite), FCC_A1 (austenite) and BCC_A1#2 (high-Mn BCC) (BLOCK b0016, b0027, b0033).

After deformation at 500 °C to true strain 0.6, SEM composition analysis (Table 1) gave Mn = 10.3±0.1 wt% in ferrite and 12.8±0.1 wt% in austenite, and Al = 6.0±0.1 wt% in ferrite and 4.7±0.1 wt% in austenite (BLOCK b0035).
The alloy has a reported stacking fault energy of 80–110 mJ/m^2, which makes deformation-induced austenite-to-martensite transformation theoretically impossible (BLOCK b0013).

The thermodynamic analysis (identical Gibbs free energy of BCC and FCC at the partitioned compositions) is presented for isothermal sections of 500 °C and 550 °C, but the deformation experiments themselves were conducted at 500 and 600 °C (BLOCK b0028, b0033).
